per_claim.claim: CNN surrogate predicts outgoing spectra for single-material steel shields with ≤10 % dose error on unseen thicknesses.
per_claim.evidence: Replication shows steel dose errors 78 %–854 % for four unseen thickness cases, far above the claimed ≤10 %.

per_claim.claim: Model interpolates to unseen thicknesses and to a new material via density encoding.
per_claim.evidence: Concrete and BPE (not in training) give 6 %–23 % dose errors, within ~25 %, but steel interpolation failed; high-density concrete case of paper not reproduced.

per_claim.claim: Chaining the CNN handles multi-layer shields with agreement within a factor ≈2.
per_claim.evidence: Replication did not include multi-layer evaluation; only single-layer materials were verified.

per_claim.claim: Inference takes ~20–30 ms per sample enabling minute-scale sweeps.
per_claim.evidence: Measured 104 ms per sample—slower than claimed but still permits a 240-call sweep in 26 s; speed benefit remains but magnitude reduced.

per_claim.claim: Training converges in 20 epochs within 30–60 min on a single CPU core.
per_claim.evidence: Training completed 20 epochs in 60 s with stable loss convergence, well inside stated time window.

one_line: Replication rebuilt the CNN and found training speed consistent but key accuracy claim for steel shields failed, while interpolation and speed benefits were only partly confirmed.
notes: Differences in Monte-Carlo ground truth code (OpenMC vs PHITS) and reduced energy range (≤19 MeV) may contribute to discrepancies, but large steel errors suggest the original accuracy claim is not robust.
